name: Custom Desktop
description: A box you built yourself, and the first machine that is faster than the laptop. Takes a floor slot, so the bedroom only has room for one beside it.

name: GPU Rack
description: Massive local throughput at industrial power draw. It will not fit beside a bed, and its own fans are nowhere near enough — pair it with an immersion cooling rig.

name: Rent the Garage
description: Room for four machines, and enough extraction to run a desktop hard. Anything heavier still needs cooling of its own. Rent becomes $1,400/round.

name: Lease the Warehouse
description: Sixteen slots of industrial space, and a roof strong enough for a cooling tower. Rent becomes $8,000/round.

name: Compute Cluster
description: A rack of racks. Massive throughput over the GPU rack, at a power draw no room cools on its own — budget for an industrial chiller alongside it.

name: Garage Data Centre
description: The garage was never really for the car. Needs a chilled-water plant beside it to run safely.

name: Compute Warehouse
description: An entire warehouse of racks. This is what the datacentre campus lease was for, and what the cryogenic exchange hall exists to cool.

name: Industrial Campus
description: A campus of warehouses. The private power grid exists because the public one asked you to leave.

name: Orbital Cooling Array
description: Radiators in orbit, aimed away from the sun. Adds no throughput of its own — it exists so the rest of the campus can run flat out.

name: Rent an Office Unit
description: Eight slots, ducted air, and a landlord who will let you hang a chiller off the wall. Rent becomes $3,200/round.

name: Lease the Data Centre Campus
description: A campus built for compute warehouses. Rent becomes $150,000/round.

name: Build a Private Power Grid
description: Your own substation. Enough cooling and slots for an industrial campus. Rent becomes $900,000/round.

name: Build the Moon Facility
description: Free vacuum cooling and nobody left to complain about the noise. Rent becomes $6,000,000/round.

name: Open a Cloud Account
description: Sign up, hand over a card, and agree to terms nobody has read. Nothing else on this shelf exists until you do, and neither does the CLOUD key on the board.

name: Reserved Capacity
description: A long-term reservation at a steep discount over pay-as-you-go, in exchange for a much larger standing bill.

name: Multi-Cloud Failover
description: Redundant capacity across providers, so an outage on one is somebody else's problem.

name: "Unlimited" Enterprise Contract
description: Effectively unlimited cloud capacity. The word "effectively" is doing a great deal of work in that sentence.

name: Pay-As-You-Go Cloud
description: Immediate cloud capacity, metered by the second and billed by the round. Twice the laptop, at a price that notices you are still renting a bedroom.

name: Spot Instance Arbitrage
description: Cheap capacity bought on the spot market, with the outage risk that makes it cheap.

name: Basic Ad Campaign
description: Increase demand with daily ad spend.

name: Portable Air Conditioner
description: A hose out of the window and a tray that needs emptying. Takes no floor space, so buy as many as the room will tolerate.

name: Immersion Cooling Rig
description: A bath of dielectric fluid with a rack sitting in it. Ugly, loud, and the only thing that makes a GPU rack survivable in a garage.

name: Industrial Chiller
description: A commercial chiller bolted to the outside wall. This is the cooling a compute cluster actually needs, whatever the office lease implied.

name: Chilled-Water Plant
description: Pipework, pumps, and a cooling tower on the roof. The warehouse has the space; this is what fills it with cold.

name: Cryogenic Exchange Hall
description: A hall of heat exchangers running on liquid nitrogen. Campus-scale compute makes campus-scale heat, and this is where it goes.

name: Maxed-Out RAM
description: Every slot on the laptop board filled with the cheapest sticks that fit. Doubles what the machine you already own can push, and takes no floor space.

name: Second Graphics Card
description: One more card in the desktop you built. One per desktop owned, and the power supply notices.

name: Overclocking Kit
description: More clock than the silicon was sold with, and no extra cooling to go with it. One per desktop owned.

name: Rack Expansion Shelf
description: The empty U at the top of a rack you already pay rent on. One per rack owned.

name: Second Monitor
description: One more pipeline slot on the Burn Board. Turns out you could not see the whole workflow on a laptop.

name: A Second Desk
description: Room for another workflow, so a careful contract and a fast one no longer have to share a pipeline.

name: Standing Desk Setup
description: Another pipeline slot, and a posture your physiotherapist describes as 'a start'.

name: Sales Outreach
description: Invest in sales to unlock bigger contracts. Each level lowers the reputation needed for higher tiers.

name: Cloud Compute
description: Raise the ceiling on a cloud burst. Each level adds +0.5× to the burst multiplier.
